newsitem.title: USA: N.J. committee approves dissolving Trenton agency.
newsitem.headline: N.J. committee approves dissolving Trenton agency.

text.p: A New Jersey legislative committee on Monday unanimously approved a bill to dissolve Trenton's Capital City Redevelopment Corp and transfer its assets and liabilities to a new development agency.
The Assembly Commerce and Military and Veterans' Affairs Committee released the bill, which the full Senate has already approved.
The sponsor, Sen. Dick LaRossa, said it would give Trenton more flexibility in deciding how to spend development money.

"This measure will finally ensure that those with the greatest stake, those who live and work in the city of Trenton, will be given the opportunity to decide how money is spent for the promotion and revitalization of the city," LaRossa said.
Capital City Redevelopment Corp was created in 1987 with an initial appropriation of $5 million. Since then, it has operated a revolving loan pool for new projects in the city.

Under the bill, the state would transfer the assets of the state-run corporation to the new Economic Development Corp, and free up the new agency to use other sources of revenue for new projects and expand its geographic authority.
